items.followUp: State one characteristic of elements in the same group and one characteristic of elements in the same period.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of a group and a characteristic of its elements.
rubric.description: Identifies a group as a vertical column and gives a shared characteristic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a group as a vertical column and stating either that its elements have the same number of valence electrons or similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of a period and a characteristic of its elements.
rubric.description: Identifies a period as a horizontal row and states that its elements have the same number of electron shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a period as a horizontal row and stating that its elements have the same number of electron shells.

modelAnswer: A group is a vertical column in the periodic table; its elements have the same number of valence electrons and similar chemical properties.
A period is a horizontal row; its elements have the same number of electron shells.

items.followUp: Explain why ionization energy increases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Links the increased nuclear attraction across a period to the energy required to remove an electron.
rubric.description: Explains the increase in ionization energy across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that effective nuclear charge increases while the outer electrons remain in the same shell, so more energy is needed to remove an electron.

rubric.why: Links the greater distance and shielding down a group to weaker attraction for the outer electron.
rubric.description: Explains the decrease in ionization energy down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that additional shells increase the distance and shielding of the outer electron, decreasing nuclear attraction and the energy needed to remove it.

modelAnswer: Across a period, effective nuclear charge increases while the outer electrons remain in the same shell, so attraction to the nucleus increases and more energy is needed to remove an electron.
Down a group, additional shells increase the distance and shielding of the outer electron, so the nuclear attraction decreases and less energy is needed to remove it.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?

rubric.why: Identifies the strong attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds contain oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying positively and negatively charged ions and their strong electrostatic attraction.

rubric.why: Explains that the ions are held in an ordered, rigid arrangement in the solid.
rubric.description: States that the ions form a rigid crystal lattice, making the compound solid at room temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ions form a rigid crystal lattice or are held in fixed positions.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds consist of positively and negatively charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
The ions are arranged in a rigid crystal lattice, so ionic compounds are solid at room temperature.

items.followUp: State two factors that can cause an element to show allotropy.

rubric.why: Identifies differences in the number of atoms in molecules as one cause of allotropy.
rubric.description: States that allotropes may have different numbers of atoms in their molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning different numbers of atoms in the molecules of an element.

rubric.why: Identifies differences in atomic arrangement as another cause of allotropy.
rubric.description: States that allotropes may differ in the arrangement of atoms in their structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a different arrangement of atoms in the structure of an element.

modelAnswer: Allotropy may be caused by different numbers of atoms in the molecules of an element.
It may also be caused by different arrangements of atoms in the structure of the element.

items.followUp: Which solution is more concentrated: 0.5 M or 2 M? Explain briefly.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the more concentrated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for choosing the three-molar (3 M) solution.

rubric.why: Checks understanding that concentration compares the amount of solute in a given volume of solution.
rubric.description: Explains that the three-molar solution has more solute per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains 3 moles of solute per litre, compared with 1 mole per litre in the one-molar solution.

modelAnswer: The three-molar (3 M) solution is more concentrated.
It contains 3 moles of solute per litre of solution, whereas a one-molar solution contains 1 mole per litre.
